proof:
# Four fibers with identical middle bodies

Let K be any full-dimensional compact convex body in R^d, with centroid g and volume V. Let A,C be full-dimensional convex subsets of K with volumes a,c. Put the four fibers

    A, K, K, C

at consecutive integer bases 0,1,2,3. Their convex hull has exactly these integer fibers. In particular every convex combination of source points landing at a middle base has its continuous point in K, while the exposed endpoint fibers remain A and C.

Write `Gamma=Gamma_d`. Choose

    y=(1,g) if a>=c,       y=(2,g) if c>=a.

Then EVERY original closed containing ambient halfspace has mass at least

    Gamma V + (1/2) max(a,c)
      >= (Gamma/2)(2V+a+c).                           (1)

This holds for all d>=1, all endpoint shapes and translations within K, and every common continuous normal and integer tilt.

## 1. Proof at the selected actual point

If a>=c, use the proved measurable-subset inequality on the THREE actual sources A,K,K at bases 0,1,2. At `(1,g)` it supplies `Gamma V+a/2` for every containing cap. The fourth source contributes nonnegative mass. This retains one actual cap normal and tilt throughout; the threshold offsets on the selected triple are opposite about its middle point.

If c>=a, reverse the triple K,K,C and use the same theorem at `(2,g)`. Again the unused endpoint contributes nonnegative mass. Vertical caps contain the whole selected middle K and at least one whole source of that triple, so the same bounds hold. A containing cap includes its parallel through-point cap.

Finally `max(a,c)>=(a+c)/2` and `Gamma<=1/2` give (1). More quantitatively the excess over the target is at least

    ((1-2Gamma)/4)(a+c).                              (2)

This is positive for d>=2. We have chosen one of two individually controlled points; we have not summed two lower bounds that spend the same middle mass.

## 2. Actual homothetic chains with equal middle radii

Suppose a four-fiber actual homothetic chain has two middle fibers that are translates of the same body K. Subtract the affine-in-base map interpolating their translations, making both middle bodies identical. Actual convexity gives

    (A+K)/2 subset K,       (K+C)/2 subset K.

Taking support functions proves `A subset K` and `C subset K`. Thus the theorem applies. In particular every four-homothetic-fiber chain with equal middle radii satisfies the sharp target, without restrictions on endpoint scales or original translations. The result actually permits arbitrary endpoint shapes after the shear.

The functional dependency is `candidate dafd411c026c302c`, Section 6. An archive check found earlier four-interval midpoint failures and spatial reflection certificates, but not this arbitrary-dimensional equal-middle subset theorem.

## 3. Why two prescribed peak centroids cannot handle unrestricted tails

The requirement of exactly four fibers is substantive for the simple two-point selector. Here is an exact larger-chain obstruction, even with a common centered shape and a unique adjacent equal peak pair.

Take d=2 and any centroid-zero convex body K of volume one. At bases i=0,...,9 put fibers `r_i K`, where

    r_0=r_1=1,
    r_i=1-(i-1)/100     (2<=i<=9).

The radius sequence is positive and concave: its successive slopes are zero and then the constant `-1/100`. Piecewise-affine interpolation gives an actual convex body with these exact integer fibers and with `C_body=conv(S)`. The only maximum-radius plateau is the pair 0,1. Its total mass is

    M=2+sum_(k=1)^8 (1-k/100)^2 = 23251/2500.

The vertical caps `z<=0` and `z<=1` bound the depths of the two prescribed plateau centroids by 1 and 2 respectively, whereas

    (Gamma_2/2)M = 23251/11250 > 2,
    (Gamma_2/2)M-2 = 751/11250.                       (3)

Thus neither of those two prescribed centroids attains the target. This example does NOT impose marginal-median eligibility on the peak bases and does not settle that more restricted question.

It is explicitly safe for the original depth target: base 4 is a weighted median. The strict left mass is `39405/10000` and the strict right mass is `44190/10000`, both below `M/2=46502/10000`. At `(4,0)`, a cap captures at least a Gamma_2 fraction of every fiber whose centroid it contains. Those centroids have continuous coordinate zero, so a containing ambient cap selects a closed half-line of bases through 4, of mass at least M/2. Hence this actual point has cap mass at least `Gamma_2 M/2`.

The counterexample concerns the prescribed peak-centroid extension only. It does not rule out moving to another integer base, and it does not contradict (1).

The standard-library verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_four_fiber_equal_middle_subset.py` checks the selector arithmetic, actual rational triangular cap incidences, and the complete tail-counterexample constants.
